reasoning: One walker change (_stage_verdict) closes the observed bypass for both hooks. A RED set and preservation rows hold D1 and D2. Every shell behaviour the design rests on is observed in the proposal, and the residual is stated honestly as having no catcher beyond the default-branch ruleset.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1/D2 consider keeping the literal `-c` (rejected: `bash -c -e` stays open, observed in proposal Why) and a per-shell option grammar (rejected as Non-Goal). A third option is to stop at the first operand and look for `c` only among the leading options. It is no shorter, and it would lose `bash -o pipefail -c "…"`, which main denies today; D1 now names that case. So scanning all tokens and then taking the first operand is the minimal design that keeps current coverage.

All the named existing tests exist.

replaced.evidence: No project-declared input is replaced and no guard is dropped. The exact `-c` lookup is widened, not removed. The forms main denies today stay denied under D1/D2, including value options before `-c`, which the preservation rows now prove. The wider navigation denials are listed in design Risks.

It accepts the gap on the grounds the git_guard.py docstring states: a guardrail against agent error, not a security boundary. tasks.md 4.2 carries the same statement into the PR report.
